basics.name: Imed Kouki
basics.label: Automation Developer & Researcher
basics.summary: RPA developer combining research in LLM-driven business process modeling with industrial experience in enterprise automation using UiPath and Microsoft Power Automate. Owns the automation lifecycle end to end, from process analysis and solution design to testing, deployment, and production support, and works across REST APIs, n8n, LLMs, and agentic and multi-agent systems. Master of Research graduate with a thesis on agentic approaches to BPMN process model generation, published at ICAART 2026.

work.name: TUI Group
work.summary: Enterprise RPA and intelligent automation across the full lifecycle (analysis, design, development, testing, deployment, support) with UiPath and Power Automate.
highlights: Delivered 18+ automation projects with up to 70% reduction in processing time, 95%+ accuracy, and cumulative savings above 11 FTEs.

Streamlined a booking process of 15,000 cases per year with Power Automate, cutting handling time from 40 minutes to about 6 minutes per booking, reducing error rates, and saving an estimated 5.7 FTEs.

Led requirements-gathering and solution-design workshops with business stakeholders and analysts, and produced BPMN-aligned PDDs and SDDs in line with process governance standards and deployment pipelines.
Delivered training and knowledge-transfer sessions to client teams for smooth handover.

Built end-to-end automation workflows on UiPath (Studio, Orchestrator, Document Understanding, AI Center) and Power Automate, integrating REST APIs, Microsoft Graph, SharePoint, Dataverse, SQL Server, and Azure services.

Engineered ETL pipelines with Power Automate, PowerShell, and SQL Server to extract and transform ERP data into automated SharePoint and Dataverse workflows, and built data pipelines and document-processing workflows with n8n and custom connectors.
Established reusable UiPath component libraries and standardized testing patterns (unit, integration, mock), reducing development effort by 30-40%.
Designed agentic automation solutions with UiPath Maestro and n8n, combining AI agents, APIs, RPA workflows, and Document Understanding pipelines.
Monitored and maintained production automations, troubleshooting failures and implementing reliability and performance improvements.
Applied ALM best practices and governance using Git, GitLab, and CI/CD, and coordinated delivery in Jira (sprint planning, task tracking, defect management).

work.name: LARIA, ENSI (University of Manouba)
work.summary: Master's thesis research on agentic, LLM-driven generation of BPMN process models from natural language.
highlights: Developed agentic systems for automated BPMN process model generation using multi-agent architectures built with LangChain and LangGraph, focusing on schema validation, systematic prompting, and the reliability of text-to-model synthesis.
Built RAG pipelines with Mistral embeddings to reduce context-window dependency, and custom text-processing workflows for chunking and cleaning data before agent execution.
Prototyped pipeline orchestration with n8n through rapid experimentation.
Implemented a web-based interface with bpmn.io for BPMN visualization and interaction.
Used LangSmith for tracing, performance insights, and benchmarking of agent behavior across Mistral models (Large and Medium) and configurations.
Published the research at ICAART 2026 (18th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence).

publications.name: Automated BPMN Model Generation from Natural Language
publications.publisher: ICAART 2026 - 18th International Conference on Agents and Artificial Intelligence
publications.summary: Problem: manual construction of BPMN diagrams is time-consuming and error-prone, and this work investigates how large language models can automate it from textual process descriptions. Approach: text-to-model synthesis through systematic prompt engineering and multi-agent architectures, combined with schema validation so that generated BPMN models are syntactically well-formed and standards-compliant.
